findings.message: Section 3 still says "`runner.drive` reviews committed ticket content before Implement unless the journal already records an approval for that blob." The diff removed the ticket-SHA-only bypass. Dispatch now reuses only the latest verdict for the stem, and only when it is an approval whose recorded input identity matches the current inputs.
findings.paved_road: Update this sentence in the requisition part of section 3 to describe the input-identity reuse rule and what invalidates it.

findings.message: Criterion 1 requires proof that a confirmation-only (draft-to-confirmed) transition reuses the approval with zero extra preflight or model calls. No test in the four named files covers that transition. They only cover a second identical CLI review and a dispatch reuse with the identity gatherer mocked out.
findings.paved_road: Add an integration test that approves a draft ticket through `ticket review`, runs `ticket confirm`, then reviews or dispatches again. Assert no new requisition_review request and no new verdict event.

findings.message: Criterion 2 requires proof that changes to Context bytes, sibling material, coverage, specs or substantive ticket text force a new review. Only a tracked code edit (clutch/thing.py) is tested. The other invalidation inputs are untested, and an approval followed by a newer rma is tested only in the unit selection test, not in the named integration files.
findings.paved_road: Add integration cases that change each named input after an approval: a Context-referenced file, an overlapping sibling ticket, coverage-map.json, a spec file, and the ticket body beyond its state line. Assert exactly one new requisition_review call each. Add a newer-rma case alongside the newer-snag case.

findings.message: Criterion 3 requires proof that both entry points preserve provisional (unmerged-dependency) behavior and admission-refusal precedence when reuse is in play. No test covers either: no CLI review of a ticket with an unmerged dependency and a matching recorded approval, and no refused admission alongside a reusable approval.
findings.paved_road: Add unit or integration tests in the named files. Show that a CLI review with an unmerged dependency still runs a provisional review and journals nothing despite a matching approval, and that a refused admission still refuses with no reuse and no model call at both entry points.

findings.message: Criterion 4 requires proof that a CLI default-tier approval is reused by dispatch when tiers match, and that a reviewer-tier change forces exactly one new review. No test runs `ticket review` and then dispatches the same ticket at a matching tier. test_ladder.py only inserts extra scripted verdicts; it never asserts the requisition_review call count across a tier change.
findings.paved_road: Add an integration test that approves through `ticket review` and then drains at the default tier, asserting zero requisition_review requests at dispatch. Add a test that changes the effective tier (for example via an escalation rung) and asserts exactly one new requisition_review request.
